method.title: Soil Macrofauna Sampling
method.description: The TSBF (Tropical Soil Biology and Fertility) method is an internationally recognized protocol for assessing soil macrofauna and the biological quality of the soil.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: The method seeks to identify organisms in the soil that can indicate environmental changes, fertility and ecological balance.
objective.soilQualityDesc: Assesses ecological balance through the biodiversity present.
objective.biologicalIndicatorsDesc: Uses organisms such as earthworms, ants and beetles as bioindicators.
objective.environmentalMonitoringDesc: Allows comparison between preserved, degraded and agricultural areas.

howTo.title: How to collect
howTo.step1Desc: Select a representative point of the study area, avoiding places with recent disturbance.
howTo.step2Desc: Mark out a 25cm x 25cm monolith up to 20cm deep.
howTo.step3Desc: Carefully remove the organisms found in the litter and in the soil.
howTo.step4Desc: Classify the organisms according to the taxonomic groups available in the app.
howTo.step5Desc: Take photos in the four directions (North, South, East and West) to document the area.
howTo.step6Desc: The system will automatically calculate the density and the soil macrofauna quality index.

mainGroups.title: Main groups found
mainGroups.earthwormsDesc: Improve soil structure and increase water infiltration.
mainGroups.antsDesc: Help with nutrient cycling and soil movement.
mainGroups.beetlesDesc: Important predators and decomposers of the soil fauna.

interpretation.title: Interpreting the Overall Score
interpretation.intermediate: Intermediate quality with signs of degradation.
interpretation.low: Low biological quality and possible severe degradation.

taxonInfo.earthworm: Earthworms are key to soil structure and fertility, promoting aeration and nutrient cycling.
taxonInfo.ant: Ants contribute to nutrient cycling, seed dispersal and soil aeration.
taxonInfo.isoptera: Termites decompose lignified organic matter and are key ecosystem engineers of the soil.
taxonInfo.blattaria: Cockroaches take an active part in decomposing organic matter, helping recycle nutrients in the soil.
taxonInfo.coleoptera: Beetles have diverse ecological roles, including decomposition, predation, pollination and soil bioturbation.
taxonInfo.arachnida: Spiders are important predators that regulate populations of insects and other invertebrates in the soil and vegetation.
taxonInfo.diplopoda: Millipedes help decompose plant residues, fragmenting litter and speeding up nutrient cycling.
taxonInfo.chilopoda: Centipedes are agile soil predators that control small invertebrate populations and help balance the soil fauna.
taxonInfo.hemiptera: True bugs (Hemiptera) have varied feeding habits — plant feeders, predators or detritivores — and play distinct roles in soil food webs.
taxonInfo.dermaptera: Earwigs are omnivorous opportunists that feed on decaying organic matter, fungi and small invertebrates, helping balance the macrofauna.
taxonInfo.lepidoptera: Caterpillars are herbivorous lepidopteran larvae that affect plant biomass and, when in the soil, contribute to bioturbation and organic matter cycling.
taxonInfo.gasteropoda: Land molluscs (slugs and snails) take part in decomposing plant matter and are important links in soil food chains.
taxonInfo.diptera_larvae: Dipteran larvae (flies and mosquitoes) live in litter and soil, feeding on decaying organic matter and helping to break it down.
taxonInfo.isopoda: Isopods (woodlice) fragment litter and feed on decaying organic matter, speeding up nutrient cycling.
taxonInfo.orthoptera: Orthopterans (crickets and grasshoppers) are generally herbivores or omnivores and are part of the soil food web, serving as prey for many predators.
taxonInfo.others: Other soil organisms include springtails, mites and other invertebrates that perform varied ecological functions in the soil macrofauna.
